questions.scenarioContext: An energy supplier is developing a new smart device. There will be a portable display unit that provides information to the customer about energy usage and cost. This is connected wirelessly to a smart meter that measures the energy used by the customer. The portable display unit and smart meter will be connected to each other using Wi-Fi.
questions.prompt: Identify two characteristics of a Wi-Fi connection.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: wireless (uses radio waves, no cables), medium indoor range (~30–50m), high data transfer speed/bandwidth, supports multiple devices, can suffer interference from thick walls/obstacles, requires encryption/password for security.

questions.scenarioContext: Portable energy display unit connected to a smart meter.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the customer of the portable display unit having an HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: makes live energy usage and costs easy to read/understand visually so customers can spot high-usage appliances and reduce bills; easy to navigate menus/settings.

questions.scenarioContext: The portable display unit is small with a high-resolution HCI to show updated visual information.
questions.prompt: Explain how processing power will impact the design of the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: a small portable unit has limited CPU/processing power, so the HCI must keep graphics/animations lightweight and simple to avoid lag/freezing and excessive battery drain when refreshing live energy data.

questions.scenarioContext: Customers will be able to use touch to interact with the portable energy display unit HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to customers of using touch to interact with the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: intuitive/easy to use with no extra peripherals (keyboard/mouse) needed, keeps the portable device compact, quick to tap icons to switch between electricity/gas/cost views.

questions.prompt: Identify two other user interaction methods.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: voice, keyboard, mouse, gesture, physical buttons/dials, stylus/pen.

questions.scenarioContext:
The HCI for the portable display unit will allow customers to see their energy usage. The information shown will include the:
• total energy usage and cost for each day
• date and time
• Wi-Fi connectivity status with the meter.
questions.prompt:
Create a mind map to plan the home screen of the HCI for the portable display unit.
Marks will be awarded for: content; layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (central node 'Energy Display Home Screen', main branches for Daily Usage & Cost (kWh / £ / gas & electric), Date & Time, Wi-Fi/Meter Status (signal strength/connected icon), Navigation/Settings/Alerts/House style) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear central idea, logical branches & sub-nodes, concise keywords, well-organised readable structure).

questions.scenarioContext: The energy supplier will provide customers with access to a video with instructions about how to use the portable display unit.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the suitability of using a video to communicate this information to customers.

In your answer you must consider:
• the purpose of the video
• the advantages to customers of using the video
• the disadvantages to customers of using the video.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Purpose: demonstrate step-by-step how to set up, pair, and read the portable display unit clearly. Advantages: visual + audio demonstration easier to follow than a manual, can pause/rewind/replay, engaging, accessible with subtitles/captions. Disadvantages: requires internet access and a video-capable device (excludes less tech-savvy/elderly customers), uses bandwidth/data, harder to skim quickly for one specific setting than a printed leaflet, language/hearing barriers without subtitles. Reasoned conclusion.

questions.prompt: Identify two audience demographics that impact the distribution of the customer video.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: age, accessibility (visual/hearing needs), location (rural broadband coverage), gender, income/socio-economic status, language.

questions.scenarioContext: The data collected by the smart meter will automatically be sent to the energy supplier using the Internet of Everything (IoE).
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the energy supplier of using the IoE in energy management.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): accurate automated meter readings reduce need for staff visits/estimated bills, real-time demand forecasting helps manage grid load/detect faults. Disadvantage (2): high upfront cost to roll out smart meters/infrastructure, cyber-security/hacking risks to customer data or energy grid, connectivity outages prevent data transmission.

questions.prompt: Identify one other area of everyday life where the IoE could be used.
questions.markSchemeHint: Healthcare/fitness wearables, smart homes (heating/security/appliances), transport/smart vehicles, education, retail, emergency services, banking, agriculture.

questions.scenarioContext: The data collected by the energy supplier will be stored on a network drive.
questions.prompt: Identify two characteristics of a network drive that make it suitable to store the energy data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: large storage capacity for millions of readings, centralised/shared access for authorised staff across the organisation, easier centralised backups, controlled user permissions/security, scalable.

questions.scenarioContext: The data collected by the smart meter is stored on the network drive.
questions.prompt: Complete the table to show the data types that will be used to store the data. Justify each of your choices.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 data type + 2 justification): Connectivity (on/off) -> Boolean (only two possible states: on/off or true/false, minimal storage & prevents invalid input); Energy usage (8.65) -> Real / Decimal / Float (numeric value with decimal places allowing precise calculations/totals); Cost of energy (2.74) -> Currency (monetary value formatted to 2 decimal places with £ symbol for billing calculations).

questions.scenarioContext: The data contained on the network drive is at risk from cyber-security threats, including data manipulation.
questions.prompt: Describe what data manipulation is.
questions.markSchemeHint: Unauthorised changing, altering, or tampering with stored/transmitted data (1) to falsify records, disrupt operations, or cause harm/financial gain (e.g., altering customer energy bills) (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Logical prevention measures will be used to increase the protection of the data stored on the energy supplier's network drive.
questions.prompt: Explain how access rights and permissions and anti-virus software could be used to keep the data secured.
questions.markSchemeHint: Access rights & permissions (2): restricts who can view, edit, or delete energy data based on staff job roles (e.g., read-only vs admin), limiting insider threat and accidental changes. Anti-virus software (2): continuously scans files/network traffic to detect, quarantine, and remove malware/viruses before they corrupt or steal stored data.

questions.scenarioContext: When a customer leaves an energy supplier their stored data must be removed from the network drive.
questions.prompt: Describe what data erasure is.
questions.markSchemeHint: Using specialist software to permanently overwrite/remove all traces of data on a storage medium (1) so the customer's data cannot be recovered while leaving the drive reusable (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Removing former customer data from a magnetic hard drive.
questions.prompt: Describe how magnetic wipe can be used to securely destroy data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Exposes the magnetic storage drive to a very strong magnetic field (degaussing) (1) which demagnetises/scrambles the magnetic platters so stored data is permanently erased and unrecoverable (1).
